issues.legal_issue: Displacement through lawful land acquisition does not give every adult member of a displaced family or later descendants a constitutional entitlement to employment or preferential employment.
material_facts: Land was acquired for the construction of a public steel plant, and compensation was paid.
The petitioners sought employment for every adult member of displaced families, including descendants, or preferential consideration when vacancies arose.

The respondents stated that 4,557 displaced persons had been employed, although about 2,901 families were affected, and the petitioners did not provide details showing that a family member had been denied the employment offered under the scheme.
issues.conclusion: The Constitution does not require employment for every member or descendant of a displaced family. The claim under Article 21 lacked merit, and extending the claimed preference would be contrary to Article 14.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Article 21 and the explanation of the right to livelihood in Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation, (1985) 3 SCC 545, the Court held that land taken through the procedure established by law and compensated for does not create a State obligation to provide employment to every affected person. The obligation to protect livelihood does not extend to guaranteeing employment to all members of each displaced family; the Court also considered such a broad preference inconsistent with Article 14.

predicates.constitutional_claim_for_displacement_ba: A person brings a constitutional claim seeking employment because land was acquired and the person or their family was displaced.
predicates.land_taken_through_lawful_process: The land was acquired by following the procedure established by law.
predicates.compensation_paid_for_land: Compensation was paid for the acquired land.
predicates.claim_seeks_employment_for_every_family_: The claim seeks employment for every affected family member or for later descendants, rather than limited assistance to the family.

issues.definition: When a constitutional employment claim arises from displacement after lawful acquisition and payment of compensation, a demand for employment for every family member or descendant does not produce a fundamental right to that employment.

issues.legal_issue: An assurance to provide employment to displaced families does not entitle every member or descendant of each family to employment when the assurance was limited to one family member and was fulfilled.
material_facts: A government statement and a ministerial recommendation were relied on as assurances of employment for displaced persons.

The ministerial recommendation was that at least one person from each displaced family could be provided a job; the judgment records that there was no specific government scheme to employ every displaced person.

The respondents stated that they had employed more displaced persons than the number of affected families, and the petitioners did not establish that the one-person-per-family commitment remained unfulfilled.
issues.conclusion: The assurance did not require employment for every displaced person or descendant; the commitment to accommodate one person from each displaced family had been satisfied.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the ministerial recommendation as a fair measure for displaced families, not a scheme guaranteeing a job to every displaced person. It found the one-person-per-family commitment fulfilled and therefore rejected a claim to employment beyond that assurance. The judgment does not cite a separate authority for this conclusion.

predicates.claim_based_on_employment_assurance: A person seeks employment on the basis of a government or employer assurance made to displaced people.
predicates.assurance_limited_to_one_member_per_disp: The assurance provides for employment of at least one person from each displaced family, rather than every member.
predicates.one_member_employment_commitment_fulfill: The employer has fulfilled the commitment to provide employment to one person from each displaced family.

issues.definition: Where an employment assurance for displaced families is limited to one person per family and that commitment has been fulfilled, the assurance does not entitle every family member to employment.

issues.legal_issue: An employer should accelerate the phased absorption of identified eligible displaced candidates when the existing pace risks delaying their employment beyond an applicable age limit.
material_facts: The employer stated that it had identified 247 displaced persons as eligible for employment and that about 50 had already been absorbed.
The employer proposed phased absorption, under which only a portion of the identified candidates would be employed each year.
The candidates were subject to an upper age limit, and the Court considered that the proposed pace could prolong their wait.
issues.conclusion: The Court considered it appropriate for the employer to expedite the absorption of the identified candidates by increasing the annual proportion taken on.
issues.legal_principle: In considering relief for the identified eligible candidates, the Court relied on the delay inherent in the proposed phased absorption and the candidates’ age limit. It directed acceleration of absorption; no earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this direction.

predicates.court_considering_relief_for_displaced_j: A court is considering relief concerning employment for displaced candidates.
predicates.employer_has_identified_eligible_displac: The employer has identified displaced candidates as eligible for employment.
predicates.employer_uses_phased_absorption: The employer plans to absorb the eligible candidates in stages rather than all at once.
predicates.candidates_face_an_age_eligibility_limit: The candidates may become ineligible for employment if their wait continues beyond an age limit.

issues.definition: When a court considers relief for identified eligible displaced candidates who are being absorbed in stages and face an age limit, the employer should expedite their absorption.
